title: `~=` accepts non-ASCII look-alike letters in pre/post-release words, then fails on matching
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

A `~=` specifier accepts a version that no other operator (and `Version`) accepts, and the resulting object is broken.

```python
from packaging.specifiers import Specifier
s = Specifier("~=1.2.3po\u017ft1")   # U+017F LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S
s.contains("1.2.3.post1")
```
Expected: `InvalidSpecifier: Invalid specifier: '~=1.2.3poſt1'` at construction, as `==1.2.3poſt1`, `>=1.2.3poſt1` and `Version("1.2.3poſt1")` already do.
Actual: the specifier is accepted, and `contains()` then fails with a bare `AssertionError`.

`Specifier("~=1.2.3prev\u0131ew1")` (U+0131 dotless i) is accepted the same way. PEP 440 versions are ASCII: non-ASCII characters must be rejected in the pre-, post- and dev-release parts of a `~=` version just as for the other operators.
acceptance: ASCII spellings such as `~=1.2.3post1`, `~=1.2.3preview1` and `~=1.2.3.dev1` stay valid
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
